newsitem.title: UK: Gold leads precious prices lower as confidence drains.
newsitem.headline: Gold leads precious prices lower as confidence drains.

text.p: Gold prices stumbled back down to recent fresh lows on Wednesday, dragging other precious metals lower in markets drained of confidence, dealers said.

"Gold is still continuing its weakening trend, but ahead of Thanksgiving, people don't want to take new positions and we should see some support at $372, so we've probably seen the lows for now," a London-based dealer said.
The New York markets are closed on Thursday and Friday for the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday. The Nymex/Comex precious and base metal future markets closed at 1800 GMT on Wednesday.
Gold, which has shed $10 in a month under selling pressure from producers and investment funds, fixed at $373.00 an ounce, a fresh low since January 1995, versus $373.95 in the morning.
"The market is so bearish right now, there's got to be a realistic chance of a further shake-out," said analyst Rhona O'Connell of stockbroker T. Hoare and Co.
The rest of the precious metals -- silver, platinum and palladium -- have become casualties of gold's weakness.
Silver fixed at a fresh 20-month low of $4.74 an ounce, and traded as low as $4.70, dealers said.

Platinum sank lower in the afternoon at $376.35 an ounce, its lowest since December 7, 1993, from $377.75 earlier and palladium also weakened to fix at $114.50 in the afternoon, a fresh low since April 20, 1993.
"There's nothing fundamental pushing platinum and palladium lower. They're just being sucked down by the bearish sentiment surrounding gold," a London-based dealer said.
On the London Metal Exchange copper held the spotlight as benchmark three months delivery snapped higher against a background of speculative short-covering on nearby spreads.
Speculative borrowing dominated as investors eyed sensitive December delivery dates where available supply was tight, traders said.
Other metals failed to match the gains in copper, with some drifting below Tuesday's closing levels and aluminium after peaking at $1,556 drifted back under profit-taking.
The soft commodities were quiet with white sugar futures setting the tone in light activity.
"There is a lot of sugar around and it (the weakness) is just a continuation of that," said one trader.
Coffee could not recover from morning losses after an uninspiring performance in New York while cocoa's early rally was met by origin sales and lack of followthorugh from New York.
The London markets will close at 1700 GMT on Thursday and Friday.
A drop in nearby wheat contracts pressured CBOT corn futures lower by the Chicago midsession, traders said.
But trading was quiet and volume thin before Thanksgiving. Markets are due to close early Wednesday at 1210 CST and also close early Friday at 1210 CST.
Corn was 1-1/4 cents lower to one cent higher, with December down 1-1/4 at $2.72.
Wheat lost ground on news Sri Lanka and Morocco had bypassed the U.S. in their wheat purchases this week. "The U.S. isn't getting any of the business," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
The purchases were made with Australai and Argentina.
Wheat was 5-1/2 cents per bushel lower to two cents higher, with December down six at $4.07 a bushel.
